name: Burg Tratzberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Tratzberg near Stans: magnificent Late Gothic and Renaissance castle with a 46 m Habsburg family tree, armory, and slow tourist train.
oeffnungszeiten: Ende März bis Anfang Nov: Mi–So 10:00–16:00 Uhr (Mo/Di Ruhetag)
beschreibung:
Overview

The magnificent Schloss Tratzberg is perched on a wooded rocky ridge high above the Tyrolean Inn Valley between Stans and Jenbach at an altitude of around 620 meters. As one of Austria's best-preserved and architecturally most significant Renaissance castles, the estate embodies the transition from medieval fortress to elegant noble palace. Completely furnished and decorated with original pieces, the property offers fascinating insights into the courtly lives of emperors, merchants, and nobles during the golden age of Tyrolean silver mining.

History & Architecture

First mentioned in the 13th century as a border fortification against Bavaria, the original fortress burned down completely in 1492. Emperor Maximilian I. initially used the ruins for his court hunts before exchanging the site in 1499 for Burg Berneck with the wealthy Schwaz mining entrepreneurs Veit-Jakob und Simon Tänzl. From 1500 onwards, the Tänzl brothers built an expansive, four-wing Late Gothic residential palace. In 1554, the powerful Augsburg merchant patrons Georg und Anton Fugger acquired the castle and redesigned it in the Renaissance style: they created the magnificent inner courtyard with delicate grisaille paintings and the elaborately wood-paneled Fuggerstube. Since 1848, the castle has been in the private ownership of the Counts of Enzenberg (today Goëss-Enzenberg), who maintain it with great devotion. The art-historical highlight is the monumental Habsburgersaal with a 46-meter-long wall frieze depicting 148 portraits of the ancestors of Maximilian I. Also remarkable are the Königinzimmer, crafted entirely without iron nails, and the completely preserved armory featuring original weapons from the 15th and 16th centuries.

Visit & Getting There

Schloss Tratzberg is open seasonally from late March to early November, Wednesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 16:00 (closed on Monday and Tuesday; last admission at 16:00). Visits take place as part of an approximately one-hour guided tour with an elaborately staged audio drama guide (in 9 languages; separate fairytale tour for children). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €18.00, youth (ages 13–17) €12.50, children (ages 4–12) €9.50, family ticket €47.50. Getting there by public transport: ÖBB train to Jenbach express station or Schwaz station, then by VVT bus route 601 directly to the Stans Tratzberg stop. By car: Inntal Autobahn A12, exit at Schwaz or Jenbach, follow the B171 to Stans; large visitor parking lot at the Schlosswirt inn (Tratzberg 1). From the parking lot, an approximate 15-minute walk through the forest or the slow tourist train Tratzberg-Express (€2.00 per ride) leads to the castle gate.

Tips

Due to heritage preservation, the castle interior with its historic wooden and stone floors and staircases is not wheelchair accessible; the Schlosswirt inn down in the valley has step-free access. Combine your castle visit with a hike through the wildly romantic Wolfsklamm gorge in Stans up to the rock monastery of St. Georgenberg. The outdoor beer garden of the Schlosswirt at the valley parking lot invites you to savor traditional Tyrolean cuisine and refreshments.
